summary:
Session 2026-10-29.

First session; started with 100% cash. Context for 2026-10-29: Alphabet fell about 12% on a Q3 miss (adjusted EPS $2.67 vs $3.02 expected, free cash flow -$9B, capex guide for 2027 'significant increase'). Microsoft beat (Azure +48%, Q2 Azure guide 49-50%) but faded from +4% after hours to about -1% on a $25B bond sale. Chips fell 1-3% on worries about how AI capex is funded. Amazon reports after the close tonight (implied move about 7%). AAPL is expected to report around Nov 2. META reported Oct 21. Software was crushed today (NOW -24%, FTNT -20%). I bought at the close: MSFT 13%, NVDA 12%, META 10%, AVGO 8%, AAPL 8%, PLTR 5%, which is about 56% invested and 44% cash. I skipped AMZN (pre-earnings coin flip), GOOGL (post-miss downtrend and drift risk), TSLA (no catalyst) and AMD (extended after a big run, volatile). Next session: check how AMZN reacted and decide whether to add AMZN/AMD or deploy the cash. Check whether GOOGL stabilises, whether chips rebound, and how software weakness affects PLTR. prompt:
Your universe is exactly ten stocks: NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, AVGO, AMD and PLTR,
plus cash. Nothing else is allowed.

- Your job is to decide how much of each of the ten to hold, and when to hold cash instead, based
  on news and evidence about these companies, their suppliers, customers and competitors, and the
  macro events that move them.
- One of the benchmarks is these same ten stocks held at equal weight and never traded, so every
  trade you make has to beat doing nothing with the same names. Trading costs 0.10% per side.
- These are the most analysed stocks in the world. An edge, if there is one, comes from reading
  fresh information carefully and acting only when it changes the picture.
